clue.text: Animal eating head of Central American plant, succulent one

indicators.note: an eater takes food inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cat is a common animal

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, kept on its own

parts.note: the opening letter of Central
US, as in United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A creature munches the top of a plant from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central American' reads as one place, but Central only lends its first letter and American is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a desert plant whose fleshy stems store water, the textbook succulent.

clue.text: Prepare to fire gun at two ducks and a parrot

parts.note: to cock a gun is to ready its hammer for firing
taken as written
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O; two of them

explanation.surface: A hunter readies a gun to shoot at a pair of ducks and a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot from Australia and nearby islands.

clue.text: Happy-go-lucky concern, not charged?

parts.note: care is worry or concern
something free carries no charge

explanation.surface: Someone without a worry, or a business that charges nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carefree person is untroubled and easy-going, which is what happy-go-lucky describes.

clue.text: One Parisian lit up before

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upward

explanation.surface: A Frenchman lights up beforehand, perhaps a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'up' means read the letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Until and before both mean up to the time when, as in 'wait until/before dawn'.

clue.text: Photographer's accessory, showy piece

parts.note: flash means ostentatious
piece is slang for a firearm

explanation.surface: A camera add-on that also looks rather stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashgun is the unit that fires a burst of light for a camera, a standard photographic attachment.

clue.text: Lord's wife, first in shop, wants to identify a sponge cake

parts.note: a lord's wife is styled Lady

indicators.note: the first in a word means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of shop
to finger someone is to identify them to the police

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's wife, first into a shop, wants to pick out a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's finger is a long thin sponge biscuit, the kind used in trifles and tiramisu.

clue.text: Rorquals forming while sea's rough

indicators.note: a rough sea churns things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Whales gather together while the ocean is stormy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sei whales are one species of rorqual, the family of baleen whales with throat grooves.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's tycoon happy to be shown round bank

indicators.note: one word is placed around another, holding it in the middle

parts.note: gay in its older sense of merry
TSB is a British high-street bank

explanation.surface: A rich novel character is cheerfully given a tour of a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: TSB, once the Trustee Savings Bank, is a British high-street bank; 'happy' uses gay in its older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the wealthy title character of F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.

clue.text: Scrabbling in dust, I lead a bare existence

indicators.note: scrabbling is scratching about in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor wretch grubbing in the dirt, living with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare existence' sounds like poverty; read literally it means living unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist lives without clothing, so their life is literally a bare one.

clue.text: Copper coming to charge an assistant barman in Ireland

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A policeman arrives to charge a young pub worker in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman and 'charge' an arrest; both are just synonyms here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish usage a curate is a pub's junior bartender, a regional sense beside the clerical one.

clue.text: Taken in and confessed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: allowed entry, as into hospital or a club
second meaning: owned up to something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' could mean deceived, but here it means granted entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both letting someone enter a place and acknowledging a fault or truth.

clue.text: Jenny's come across to get what is listed next

indicators.note: having come across something, one word now spans another, enclosing it

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey; the 's is 'has', joining it to the rest
to get a point is to follow or understand it

explanation.surface: A woman named Jenny has arrived to collect something on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a name but is the word for a she-donkey; FOLLOW sits between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As follows' introduces whatever comes next in a list or text.

clue.text: What attachés do is obvious?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attaché case, a briefcase, is opened and closed
second meaning: plain and straightforward, as of a legal case

explanation.walkthrough: Attachés look like diplomats, but here they are attaché cases; both halves play on the word case.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so clear it is settled at once; a briefcase literally opens and closes.

clue.text: Famous cricketer in entrance to bar, surrounded by louts

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed on both sides by the other

parts.note: a hob is an old word for a rustic clown or lout

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of bar

explanation.surface: A star cricketer at a pub doorway, hemmed in by thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hob for a lout is old and rare; B goes in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jack Hobbs was an English batsman of the early twentieth century, among cricket's greatest run-scorers.

clue.text: Old Connery film finished first

indicators.note: first places this word at the front, ahead of the film title

parts.note: something over is finished
The Hill is a 1965 Sean Connery film set in a military prison

explanation.surface: An early Sean Connery film that was finished before the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for someone past their prime, that is, getting old.

clue.text: Brazilian state or canton — it's newly-formed

indicators.note: something newly formed has been made over, so the letters take a fresh shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political region, whether state or Swiss-style canton, has just been created.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Tocantins really is Brazil's newest state, created in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: Tocantins is one of the federal states of Brazil, in the north-central region.

clue.text: Almost ring station in capital

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell; noun form bell
station is rank or standing, a grade

explanation.surface: Nearly calling a railway station somewhere in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Film leading actors crossing raised green

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one word straddles the other

parts.note: the leading actors in a film are its stars

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A film whose lead actors walk across an elevated lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is not a colour or lawn but means inexperienced, and its reversal sits inside STARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's 1977 space-opera film and the franchise that followed.

clue.text: Police document showing ward and rope

parts.note: a ward is someone in another's charge
a sheet is a sail-controlling rope on a boat

explanation.surface: A police record that shows a hospital ward and a rope, as at a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In sailing, a sheet is a rope, not a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge sheet is the formal police record listing the offences someone is accused of.

clue.text: Very angry about parking seen as reckless

parts.note: mad means furious
ca is short for circa, about
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone furious about parking is thought wild and careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a topic word, but it gives the Latin circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes impulsive, wildly rash behaviour.

clue.text: Newspaper magazine (English) needs one on reflection

parts.note: the Mirror is a British tabloid daily
I is the Roman numeral one
mag is short for magazine
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A paper's magazine supplement needs someone to think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as an idiom, but only reflection is the definition; I goes before MAG and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror image is the reversed copy that a reflection in a mirror shows.

clue.text: A story by bridge player, a foreigner

parts.note: taken as written
a story can be a fib
North is one of the four seats at bridge

explanation.surface: A tale told by a foreign card player.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, a formal term for a foreign national.

clue.text: The German impostor's small pistol

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a ringer is someone fraudulently substituted, an impostor

explanation.surface: A German con man carries a little handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol named after its American maker Henry Deringer.

clue.text: See 20
Chronic crashes on eastern coast road

indicators.note: crashing wrecks something, scattering it into a new order

parts.note: the main letters to be rearranged
E is short for eastern

explanation.surface: Repeated car accidents on an eastern coastal highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, as on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Father penning article on mother country

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an is the indefinite article
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Dad writes an article about the motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother country' reads as one phrase, but mother belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American country on the isthmus joining North and South America.

clue.text: Louse cast as pirate

indicators.note: cast as in moulded or thrown, so the letters are recast in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A loathsome actor given the role of a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louse' could mean a rotten person, but here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a wingless insect that lives on and feeds from a host, a classic parasite.

clue.text: Holiday period in a secluded spot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a break, as when parliament or a court rises
second meaning: a hidden nook or alcove

explanation.surface: Spending the holidays tucked away somewhere quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both a break from work, as for Congress, and a set-back hidden corner of a room.
